bull.b: Zeta is demonstrating durable demand through sustained high growth, larger enterprise relationships and broader product adoption. Rising customer use cases and ARPU support recurring expansion within the installed base and strengthen long-term revenue visibility.

bull.t: Strong Cash Generation and Margin Improvement
bull.b: Improving EBITDA margins and robust free cash flow indicate operating leverage as Zeta scales. Strong cash conversion can fund product investment, acquisitions and debt management while reducing reliance on external capital to support growth.

A large proprietary data asset, extensive model training and rising AI adoption can differentiate Zeta’s platform and improve campaign outcomes. Higher retention among AI users supports durable customer value, cross-selling and competitive positioning.

bear.t: GAAP Profitability Is Not Yet Durable
bear.b: Despite progress toward break-even, inconsistent GAAP profitability leaves Zeta more exposed to cost overruns, execution issues and changes in revenue mix. The company must convert scale and cash generation into sustained bottom-line earnings.

Growth in lower-margin social-channel activity can dilute platform economics if it becomes a larger revenue component. Persistent mix pressure could limit gross-margin expansion and reduce the operating leverage expected from Zeta’s growth.

bear.t: Growth Relies Partly on M&A and Longer Sales Cycles
bear.b: A meaningful gap between reported and organic growth increases dependence on acquisitions for headline expansion. Longer enterprise sales cycles for ZBI may also defer monetization, making growth timing and integration execution more variable.
